title: Close assertOrderEditable TOCTOU by carrying the guard into writes

acceptanceCriteria.description: The canonical order-editable write owner locks the target order row, recomputes effective lifecycle truth inside the same transaction, rejects terminal orders, and invokes the protected write callback only while the row remains editable.

Twenty-five deterministic stale-preflight races flip the order to shipped before the final PATCH transaction; every attempt fails closed with locked, invokes the protected callback zero times, and creates zero order-overrides.

All seven guarded order-write routes retain assertOrderEditable preflight and pass its writeAuthorization into withOrderEditableWrite: PATCH /:id, residential, selected-pid, selected-package-id, best-rate, shipped-external, and save-dims.
Ordinary awaiting-shipment behavior is unchanged: the protected callback runs once and persists one override when the final in-transaction lifecycle check remains editable.

Shipped/cancelled protections were not weakened: src/routes/orders.ts, assertOrderEditable, LOCKED_STATUSES, schemas, migrations, frontend locks, and runtime provider/label behavior are unchanged. The only locked runtime file touched exposes the existing transaction boundary for exact behavioral proof and retains its production wrapper.
The complete 52-command source-of-truth pack, lifecycle regressions, auth/RBAC gates, strict TypeScript, rate source-of-truth gate, and production web build pass at the reviewed SHA.

The exact reviewed SHA is live on the Render production API and fulfillment worker; public health and readiness return HTTP 200, and no ticket-specific production mutation or external provider action was performed.

canonicalOwners: src/services/order-editable-write.ts#withOrderEditableWriteInTransaction owns the row lock, in-transaction lifecycle recheck, fail-closed result, and authorization of the protected write callback
src/services/order-effective-lifecycle.ts remains the unchanged canonical owner of effective terminal lifecycle truth
src/routes/orders.ts remains a thin transport: it performs the unchanged early assertOrderEditable response check and passes the resulting writeAuthorization into the canonical write owner

oldOwners.path: The seven route-level assertOrderEditable preflight reads
oldOwners.delegatesTo: src/services/order-editable-write.ts for the authoritative final lifecycle decision at the write boundary

wrappers.delegatesTo: withOrderEditableWriteInTransaction after opening the production database transaction; it adds no lifecycle policy or fallback

sotBypass.details: The extraction exposes the existing canonical transaction boundary for deterministic testing. Production and all seven routes continue to use the same backend owner; no frontend, route helper, cache, provider adapter, or alternate lifecycle source can authorize the write.

evidence.proves: The production transaction wrapper delegates to the extracted canonical boundary, which retains FOR UPDATE row locking and effective-lifecycle recheck. Exactly the seven required route handlers retain assertOrderEditable and pass guard.writeAuthorization to the owner.

In an in-memory PostgreSQL-compatible fixture, 25 controlled interleavings make a route preflight observe awaiting_shipment and then commit shipped before the final transaction. Every final guard reports locked, the callback count remains zero, and no override row exists; the editable control persists exactly one row.

caveats.description: Two read-only /health/deep checks returned HTTP 503 solely because two order-sync accounts were stale or failed. The ticket-regression concern is closed: both exact-SHA deployments are live, /health and /health/ready are HTTP 200, database/write/event-loop/print-worker/fulfillment-outbox components are healthy, the fulfillment worker emitted no post-deploy errors, and PS-451 does not touch sync scheduling, account state, providers, or fulfillment processing. The continuing account-freshness condition is an operations follow-up outside PS-451.
